n: Vision three: a man with a measuring line in his hand.
He is going to measure Jerusalem’s width and length — perhaps to plan its walls.
The interpreting angel goes out, and another angel comes to meet him.

f.g: A second heavenly messenger with urgent news.

n: “Run, tell that young man: Jerusalem will be like an unwalled town because of all its people and animals.” The city will grow beyond any wall.

f.g: Open villages — so crowded no wall could contain them.
Probably the man with the measuring line — or Zechariah himself.

n: God Himself will be a wall of fire around Jerusalem and the glory within it. His presence is better protection than stone.

f.w: the glory in the midst of her

n: “Come out! Flee from the north country!” Many Jews still lived in Babylon (north by the travel route). God calls the scattered to come home.
Escape, Zion, you who live with Babylon! A call to leave behind the world and come to God’s city — echoed in latter-day revelation.
Whoever touches God’s people touches the apple of His eye — the pupil, the most sensitive part. God feels harm done to His people as harm done to Himself.

f.g: The pupil — something precious and fiercely protected.

f.w: he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye

n: God will wave His hand against the oppressors, and they will be plundered by their former slaves. Then you’ll know the Lord sent this messenger.
Sing and rejoice, Zion! The Lord says, “I am coming, and I will live among you.” Christians hear in this the promise of Christ dwelling among His people.

f.w: Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion
I will dwell in the midst of thee

n: Many nations will join themselves to the Lord and become His people. The gospel is for all.

f.w: many nations shall be joined to the LORD

n: The Lord will claim Judah as His special portion in the holy land and choose Jerusalem again. This is the only place in the Bible where the phrase “holy land” appears.

f.g: The only use of this exact phrase in the Bible.

n: Let all humanity be silent before the Lord, for He is rising from His holy dwelling to act.

f.w: Be silent, O all flesh, before the LORD
